_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED into src/data/index.ts. AF/G.22 population-priority push, 2026-08-13. Sub-national/regional Somalia fiscal documentation pass: adds Puntland's genuine, actively-maintained Federal Member State budget archive, the Federal Government of Somalia's FY2025 Budget Framework Paper and Financial Governance Reports apparatus (the latter two chosen specifically because they are the real, verified documents touching Benadir Regional Administration — as distinct from a fabricated figure caught and rejected mid-research), and Somaliland's Ministry of Finance & Economic Development portal (self-declared distinct administration, flagged as such). Benadir/Mogadishu municipal government itself yields NO node: forensic review of bra.gov.so's full crawl history shows the domain never held authentic budget content, only recycled WordPress-theme placeholder text.

reports.title: Puntland Ministry of Finance — Budget Archive (Enacted Budgets, Appropriation Acts, Budget Framework & Outlook Papers)
reports.publisher: Puntland State Government of Somalia, Ministry of Finance
reports.region: Puntland (Federal Member State of the Federal Republic of Somalia)
reports.description: Real, currently-maintained, downloadable primary-source budget archive confirming an active state-level (Federal Member State) fiscal system for Puntland. Site navigation (mof.pl.so homepage) lists "Budget Department," "Budget Archive," "Citizen's Budget," "Budget Framework Paper," "Budget Outlook Paper," "Financial Reports 2017–2025," and "JPLG." The Budget Archive download listing (checked 2026-08-13, cross-checked against saved page source) includes: "Enacted Budget 2026" (3.35 MB), "Draft-Appropriation-Act-for-2026-Budget" (1.36 MB), "Executives-Budget-Proposal-FY26" (1.36 MB), "Puntland Budget 2020," "Puntaland Budget for 2019," and "PSS Budget Appropriation Act- Somali Version." Jurisdiction-level note: classified here as "provincial" per this file's schema convention because Puntland is a Federal Member State government, not the Federal Government of Somalia itself — Puntland identifies itself as part of the Federal Republic of Somalia (unlike Somaliland, which asserts independence), so this is a sub-national node within Somalia's federal hierarchy, not a separate country's national budget. Scope limit: this is state (FMS)-tier documentation only — no Puntland district-level (e.g. Garowe, Bosaso) government budgets were found on this site; the site's own "JPLG" (Joint Programme on Local Governance) page, which is the section that would house local/district governance-finance content, reads only "JPLG Home JPLG Coming Soon…", i.e. explicitly unpopulated as of the check date.

reports.title: Federal Government of Somalia — Budget Framework Paper for FY 2025 (revised v15)
reports.publisher: Federal Government of Somalia, Ministry of Finance
reports.description: Real, verbatim, primary-source FGS document. Page 25, paragraph 46 (own-source revenue forecast discussion), reads: "the ongoing tax enforcement drive that continues to utilize Benaadir Regional Authority's database of property ownership to register and require landlords to pay rental income tax." This documents the FGS using Benadir Regional Authority's (BRA's) property-ownership database for federal rental-income-tax collection — it is NOT a BRA-authored municipal budget or fiscal-transfer document. Explicit correction recorded here: an earlier WebFetch summary of this same PDF, produced mid-research, claimed the document contained "Benadir Regional Administration" fiscal-transfer figures in the range of $13.65M–$31.64M. This was checked directly against the extracted PDF text and found to be FABRICATED — no such figures or content exist anywhere in the document. The document's only other Benadir/Banadir-adjacent reference is to "Banadir Regional Court" (budget code 011002), a federal judicial entity unrelated to municipal finance. See this file's _dropped list for the full record of that hallucination near-miss.

reports.title: Financial Governance Reports — Inter-Governmental Fiscal Relations (FGS & FMS)
reports.publisher: Federal Government of Somalia, Ministry of Finance / Somalia Financial Governance Committee
reports.description: Real, currently active FGS-FMS intergovernmental fiscal reporting apparatus. The Financial Governance Reports listing page includes menu items "Consolidated Fiscal Reports (FGS & FMS)" and "Inter-governmental Fiscal Federalism Forum" under an "Inter-Governmental Relations" section, with recent meeting records through January 2026. The related Budget Directorate department page states: "The Department is responsible for coordinating with all Federal Member States on the draft budget, including funds in accordance with the strategic objectives, programs, activities, and strategic performance indicators." Scope limit: this apparatus is documented only down to Federal Member State (e.g. Puntland) granularity — no district- or municipal-level (e.g. Benadir/Mogadishu) fiscal-transfer mechanism is described in these FGS Ministry of Finance publications.

reports.title: Ministry of Finance & Economic Development — Official Portal (Republic of Somaliland)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance & Economic Development, Republic of Somaliland
reports.region: Somaliland (self-declared "Republic of Somaliland"; de facto separate administration in northwestern Somalia, not treated as part of the Federal Government of Somalia's own national-tier hierarchy)
reports.description: Real, active government finance-ministry site. Homepage (slmof.org) self-describes as: "Official portal of the Ministry of Finance & Economic Development, Republic of Somaliland" / "managing public finances, national budget planning, revenue collection, expenditure control, and economic policy development" — verbatim quotes confirmed against saved page source. It explicitly self-identifies as "Republic of Somaliland" (asserting sovereign statehood), which is why this node is flagged as distinct from the Federal Government of Somalia's own national-tier claims rather than merged into them; classified as "provincial" here per this file's schema convention for Somalia's de facto sub-national/parallel administrations. A related About page states: "The Ministry of Finance Development derives its mandate from the Constitution of Somaliland, which provides for proper budgetary and expenditure management of the government financial resources" — no mention of local government, district, or municipal fiscal relations appears in that mandate text. An older/parallel portal (mofd.govsomaliland.org) references Minister Dr. Saad Ali Shire and an IFMIS (Integrated Financial Management Information System) for national government finance, with no local/municipal content found there either. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: this node captures only the ministry's self-description; the site's own "Budget Documents" page (/budget/) could NOT have its actual document titles or figures extracted — it is a JavaScript/Next.js single-page application that loads its document list client-side, so static fetch tools only retrieved the app shell, not the rendered list. This is recorded as a technical/tooling limitation, not as evidence that no such documents exist — flagged inconclusive rather than NOT FOUND (see _dropped for the specific unreadable-source record).

_dropped.why: Preserved as a methodological finding per task instructions, not silently dropped. Mid-research, a WebFetch tool call against the FGS Budget Framework Paper for FY 2025 (revised v15) returned a summary claiming the document contained "Benadir Regional Administration" fiscal-transfer figures of roughly $13.65M–$31.64M. This claim was independently verified against the actual extracted PDF text (page 25, paragraph 46, and a full text search of the document) and found to be FABRICATED — no such figures, and no content resembling them, exist anywhere in the real document. The real document's only relevant content is the sentence about the FGS tax-enforcement drive using "Benaadir Regional Authority's database of property ownership" to collect rental income tax (now captured verbatim in so-fgs-budget-framework-paper-fy2025's description), plus an unrelated reference to "Banadir Regional Court" (budget code 011002, a federal judicial line item). No figure from the hallucinated summary was used anywhere in this file's report nodes.

No node minted for Benadir Regional Administration / Mogadishu municipal government finance. Verdict: NOT FOUND, with a specific documented reason. bra.gov.so's live homepage currently returns only "Sorry, we're doing some work on the site... We are doing some work on the site and will be back shortly" (checked 2026-08-13, cross-checked against saved page source, which shows no under-construction text confirming the page is presently blank/near-empty). A Wayback Machine snapshot of a page literally titled "Budget Allocation-Q3" (https://web.archive.org/web/20241114010300/https://bra.gov.so/ova_doc/budget-allocation-q3/) contains only generic Ovatheme WordPress demo/lorem-ipsum text ("We help our clients to build their best possible economic... Thomas Edison may have been behind the invention of the electric light bulb...") unrelated to any real budget. A snapshot of the Finance & Economic Planning department page (https://web.archive.org/web/20240804142134/https://bra.gov.so/departments/finance-economic-planning/) lists a placeholder contact "finance@email.com" with generic boilerplate reused verbatim across multiple department pages. Wayback CDX index for that same department page shows its last successful (200) snapshot was 2024-08-04, with a 2025-05-05 snapshot returning HTTP 404, consistent with progressive site abandonment rather than removal of real content. Combined, these confirm bra.gov.so is a government-registered domain that appears to have never held authentic financial content — a documentable "facade e-government presence" finding, not merely an absence of records. A separate World Bank ESMP document for the Benadir Urban Resilience Project II likewise contains no BRA financial statements, revenue figures, or PFM capacity assessment (only a forward-looking, non-binding reference to future district-level operating budgets), and is in any case a World Bank (non-primary) document.

SONNA (Somali National News Agency, state-owned) reported that "Banadir Municipality approves $101.3 million budget for 2025" (https://sonna.so/en/banadir-municipality-approves-101-3-million-budget-for-2025), quoting a Deputy Governor statement from a Dec 30, 2024 approval ceremony. This is the closest thing found to public confirmation that Banadir Municipality has an actual budget figure for 2025, but SONNA is a news agency, not a government-authored primary document, and the article links to no actual budget document. Excluded per the corpus evidence rule (primary government documents only); no figure from this article was used in any report node.

World Bank, "Local Governments and Federalism in Somalia: Fitting the Pieces Together" (June 2023), p.35 footnote 46, states: "The status of the Banadir Regional Administration (BRA) is yet to be defined. It either becomes the administrative capital or a fully fledged FMS. Currently, 15 percent of customs revenues is given to the BRA as a budget support." Per explicit task instruction, this World Bank report is not a primary Somali-government source and cannot be used as a corpus evidence_url — it may only be cited as context/a lead, never as evidence for a report node or dependency. No primary underlying revenue-sharing agreement or decree establishing this 15% figure could be located this round, so no node or edge was created from it.

Puntland district-level (e.g. Garowe, Bosaso) government budgets are NOT FOUND on mof.pl.so. The specific mechanism is documented: the site's "JPLG" (Joint Programme on Local Governance) page — the section that would house exactly this local/district governance-finance content — reads only "JPLG Home JPLG Coming Soon…", confirming the gap is a known, unpopulated placeholder on an otherwise well-functioning, currently-maintained ministry site, rather than the absence of any government fiscal apparatus at all.

Somaliland MOF's "Budget Documents" page (https://www.slmof.org/budget/) could not have its actual document titles or figures extracted this round. The page is a JavaScript/Next.js single-page application that loads its document list client-side; static fetch tools (WebFetch, curl) retrieved only the app shell, not the rendered document list. This is a tooling limitation, not evidence of absence — flagged inconclusive rather than NOT FOUND. A browser-rendering tool would likely surface real PDFs here in a future round.

Guessed URL https://www.slmof.org/acts-regulations returned HTTP 404. The actual Acts & Regulations page path could not be located through available tools once WebSearch quota was exhausted this round.

A UNCDF secondary article (https://www.uncdf.org/article/7867/local-government-rising-somalias-fiscal-decentralisation-success-story, not itself a primary document, cited only as a lead) references "Somaliland Law No. 23 on Regions and District Self-Government, especially Articles 88 and 89" and a "District Grants Regulation No. 01/2020" issued by Somaliland's Ministry of the Interior, and names Puntland districts Bosaso, Garowe, and Burtinle with LDF grant figures. These would be exactly the right documents to check for Somaliland's municipal/district fiscal-legal framework, but the primary text of either instrument could not be located on any Somaliland government domain within the available tool budget this round: guessed domains for a Somaliland Ministry of Interior/Local Government site (molg.gov.so, molg.govsomaliland.org, interior.govsomaliland.org, mopic.govsomaliland.org) all failed to resolve via the proxy, and www.govsomaliland.online failed with ROBOTS_DISALLOWED/DNS error. Flagged as inconclusive/needs follow-up rather than NOT FOUND, since a specific, named document trail exists and simply wasn't reachable this round.

The same World Bank report (p.37 Table 3 source line: "Source: FGS 2021 Budget Appropriation Act and FY2020 Financial Statement."; p.39 Table 5 source line: "Source: Budget execution report from the HSS Ministry of Finance website.") cites a Hirshabelle State (HSS) Ministry of Finance website as a primary source. Attempted to locate that site directly at two guessed domains (hssmof.gov.so, mof.hirshabelle.gov.so); both failed DNS/proxy resolution this round, so the HSS source could not be independently verified beyond the World Bank's citation of it, and no node was minted.

The Federal Government of Somalia's Ministry of Finance documents federal-to-Federal-Member-State (FGS↔FMS) transfers thoroughly (Budget Directorate page, Financial Governance Reports listing), but district- or municipal-level (sub-FMS) transfer mechanisms are NOT FOUND anywhere in FGS Ministry of Finance publications checked this round.

Both nodes are topically related (FGS's Budget Directorate explicitly states it coordinates with all Federal Member States, including Puntland, on the draft budget), but no FGS Ministry of Finance document reviewed this round names or cites Puntland's mof.pl.so budget archive, or any specific Puntland budget document, by title, URL, or date. Per the standing evidence rule (a verbatim textual citation is required to support a dependency edge), this is a genuine NOT FOUND for a documented citation edge despite the plausible institutional relationship.

Somalia National Bureau of Statistics CPI methodological note (https://nbs.gov.so/somalia-cpi-methodological-note/) contains genuine, verified new primary-source content not captured in this file: "Expanding geographic coverage to all Federal Member States (FMS) and Somaliland"; "In most states, data collection activities are concentrated in the capital city, whereas in Puntland, the exercise extends to three cities—Garowe, Bosaso, and Galkayo"; and a transition "from COICOP 1999 to the latest COICOP 2018 classification." This was a secondary objective of this research round and is out of scope for this file's Puntland/Benadir/MOF focus; deferred rather than incorporated, since an existing so-snbs-cpi node already exists elsewhere in the corpus (af-grok-synthesis.json) and updating it is outside this file's remit. Logged here so the finding is not lost.

Full list of guessed URLs checked that failed outright this round, for the record: https://puntlandgovernment.com, https://www.puntland.gov.so, https://mopic.puntland.gov.so, https://mofpuntland.com, https://puntland.gov.so (all failed resolution; the real Puntland MOF domain turned out to be mof.pl.so, found via search); https://molg.govsomaliland.org, https://interior.govsomaliland.org, https://molg.gov.so, https://www.molg.gov.so, https://mopic.govsomaliland.org (guessed Somaliland local-government domains, none resolved); https://hssmof.gov.so, https://mof.hirshabelle.gov.so (guessed Hirshabelle State MOF domains, none resolved); https://www.govsomaliland.online/ (ROBOTS_DISALLOWED/DNS error); https://web.archive.org/web/2024*/bra.gov.so wildcard query (PROXY_REJECTED 403, worked around via direct Wayback CDX API instead, results captured in the so-bra-municipal-budget dropped entry above).
